# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent uses 8 LUTs and 8 FFs, with no DSP48 or BRAM, and meets the 10 ns clock constraint with WNS 0.579 ns and WHS 0.052 ns. A conventional 4:1 mux already fits one LUT6 per output bit, so another Boolean rewrite offers little clear LUT savings. Explore a DSP48 resource trade instead; promotion requires fewer than 8 routed LUTs, all behavioral and independent-reference gates, successful compilation and simulation with the exact TEST PASSED verdict, SYNTH_COMPLETE, valid retained metrics, and nonnegative setup and hold slack under unchanged constraints. The supplied testbench has limited data and cycle coverage. Numeric top latency is UNKNOWN; leave the top unannotated while preserving its edge-triggered output behavior.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the LUT mux with three combinational DSP48E1 ALU selectors can reduce routed LUT usage below 8 while retaining 8 output FFs, at the cost of 3 DSP48s and two combinational DSP levels whose timing must be measured.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the four data assignments inside the clocked case with a combinational mux tree: select between a/b and c/d, then between those results, using three DSP48E1 ALUs with every internal pipeline register bypassed. Implement each selector by configuring its ALU operand multiplexers to add either zero-extended A:B data or zero-extended C data to zero, avoiding external per-bit masking; retain the original output register and its synchronous, active-high, highest-priority reset on clk. Derive deterministic selector controls through an ordinary case preserving the original default-to-d behavior for unknown selector bits, preserve all eight data bits and every observable cycle, and add no numeric latency annotation. Use only the frozen compilation environment; reject the experiment if primitive resolution, behavioral checks, routed LUT reduction, setup or hold fails, without changing libraries, constraints or the testbench.
